It seems that Elon Musk has a new utopian project, surpassing in audacity even Hyperloop and maybe even the Mission to Mars.

Why? Simply because Musk has decided to become the leading chip producer for AI in the world.

Elon Musk has just challenged all chip factories on the planet combined. According to the Emperor of Mars (Samsung + TSMC + Micron + others), they only produce 2% of what he needs right now. He made such an offer to all chip manufacturers in the world:

"I'll buy ALL of your production.
And even in that case... it's not enough for me."

That's why he is building a monster in Texas with a footprint of over 100 million square feet. The building, when completed, will become the largest and most valuable structure on Earth.

Only the first phase of the project costs $16.8 billion. His final statement leaves no room for refusal:

"Either we build Terafab... or we have no chips. And we need chips."

Terafab is a semiconductor factory (chip plant) designed to produce an absurd amount of artificial intelligence chips. The specific goal is to produce chips equivalent to 1 terawatt (1 TW) of computing power per year.

What humanity produces in decades, Musk wants to produce every year. This is no longer ambition. This is a declaration of war against scarcity.

Of course, Musk knows how to calculate, and most likely, he has already thought about where he will get terawatts of electricity every year. But the problem is that there are no such capacities in the US that can be introduced within a year.

In addition, Chinese models are already able to use orders of magnitude less power for calculations comparable in performance to leading companies in the AI field.

We live in a time when planning large investment projects, especially in the field of AI, it is no longer possible to predict how the industry will change in six months. But Musk, confident that we are living in a simulation, apparently decided to play Monopoly on a global scale.

What if one person concentrates 98% of the computational power of all AI chips in his hands, thought Musk? Such projects will certainly not allow one person to realize, whoever he may be. And in scope, the project greatly resembles the ambitions of a state striving to become great again. At the expense of others.

On-chain detective uncovers 28,555 BTC potentially linked to a historic crypto fraud

Blockchain investigator Specter has identified 28,555 BTC (≈$1.8B) that may be connected to one of the largest alleged cryptocurrency fraud cases ever.

The investigation began after a dormant wallet moved 1,020 BTC following 8 years of inactivity. Tracing the funds led to addresses associated with Zhimin Qian, whose case previously resulted in the UK seizing 61,000 BTC.

Interestingly, the newly identified wallets have remained almost completely inactive since June 2021.

It's still unclear whether these coins are controlled by the original owners, another custodian, or are already under law enforcement surveillance. For now, the massive stash remains one of the biggest dormant Bitcoin mysteries on-chain.

What does “gas” mean in crypto? 

“Gas” is important in the world of crypto. Simply put, gas is the payment needed when making a transaction or interacting with a smart contract on a blockchain — i.e., the network fee you pay. 

Gas is usually paid in the given blockchain’s native cryptocurrency — e.g., ETH is used for transactions on Ethereum, and BNB is used for the same on BNB Smart Chain). These fees go to miners or validators responsible for keeping networks secure and confirming transactions. Gas fees also prevent spam on the network, keeping the blockchain running smoothly.

🤖Still Scared AI Is Coming For Your Job? 

Here's 20 Repos To Actually Do Something About It

1. Prompt-Engineering-Guide
Explains how to actually get useful, reliable output from AI models instead of guessing and hoping.

2. AI-For-Beginners
Covers the broader AI landscape, not just LLMs, so you're not caught off guard by the next big shift either.

3. generative-ai-for-beginners
A calm, lesson-by-lesson intro to building with generative AI, no ML background assumed.

4. anthropic-cookbook
Real code examples for building things with Claude, straight from the people who make it.

5. openai-cookbook
The same idea for OpenAI's models, practical patterns instead of theory.

6. ML-For-Beginners
Twelve weeks of classic machine learning basics, useful groundwork before jumping into AI specifically.

7. llama_index
Handles connecting AI models to your own data and documents, a skill that comes up constantly in real jobs now.

8. ollama
Lets you run AI models on your own machine, good for understanding them without relying on an API key.

9. llama.cpp
Shows what's actually happening when a model runs, right down to the hardware level.

10. transformers
The library behind most modern AI models, worth exploring even just to see how they're built.

11. awesome-ai-agents
A running list of AI agent projects and frameworks, handy for keeping track of a space that moves fast.

12. nanoGPT
A small, readable implementation of GPT, built by Andrej Karpathy so you can see the whole thing without getting lost. 

13. AutoGPT
One of the earliest autonomous AI agent projects, still useful for understanding how agents plan and act.

14. gpt-engineer
An AI agent that writes entire codebases from a prompt, worth trying just to see what it's actually capable of.

15. OpenHands
An open source AI coding agent, a good look at where AI-assisted development is heading.

16. awesome-machine-learning
A broad, well-organized list of ML resources and libraries across every language, a solid reference to keep bookmarked.

17. langchain
The most widely used framework for wiring AI models into actual applications, worth knowing even if you end up not using it.

18. Awesome-LLM
A curated list of papers, models, and tools, good for going deeper once the basics feel comfortable.

19. applied-ml
Real-world write-ups from companies on how they actually use ML and AI in production, not just in demos.

20. llm-course
A structured path from "what is an LLM" to actually fine-tuning and deploying one yourself.

🚀 German Defense Minister: “Russia successfully intercepts Ukrainian Flamingo missiles”


Russia is now almost completely intercepting the Ukrainian Flamingo cruise missile. The weapon was considered Kiev's most powerful means of striking deep into the Russian hinterland.

This is reported by the Ukrainian news portal "Euromaidan Press". According to them, the Russian air force uses its remaining early warning aircraft of the Beriyev A-50u type in a targeted manner along likely flight routes in order to quickly detect missiles and direct the launch from the ground.


On the night of August 6, Ukraine fired at least three Flamingo missiles at targets in the Tyumen oblast of Western Siberia.  According to data from the Open Source observer AMK Mapping, the missiles traveled about 2500 kilometers. After that, its subsequent flight path could no longer be reconstructed. 

According to the assessment, Russia has shot ten of the eleven flamingos launched since July 1. This figure cannot be independently verified.

According to the French newspaper Indépendent, the Ukrainian attacks on important industrial facilities in Russia have therefore failed. Since July, the use of the A-50u would have changed the situation. The machines rotate over Russian territory and detect low-flying targets much earlier than ground radars.

The Flamingo cruise missile comes from the Ukrainian company Fire Point. The rocket weighs six tons, flies on a turbojet engine and reaches up to 3000 kilometers. A copy costs about $500,000, according to the Independent. 

This puts the weapon well below the price of Western cruise missiles. It also carries a 1150-kilogram warhead, the heaviest of all Ukrainian long-range weapons. 

That is why Ukraine is trying to develop the Flamingo faster, but in vain. The Firing Point would now have adjusted the altimeter so that the rocket flies even lower. The closer it stays to the ground, the more difficult it is to locate it between the earth, forests and buildings. So far, this is apparently not enough. Almost all launched flamingos are currently lost before reaching their destination.
